paragraphs: A bandit algorithm repeatedly makes choices while learning from feedback about earlier decisions. When feedback arrives late, it must act with an incomplete record of what happened. This paper proposes an algorithm for variably delayed feedback that does not require advance knowledge of the largest delay and can tolerate excessive delays as large as the decision horizon.

The method combines three technical developments. An implicit exploration scheme supports learning in the best-of-both-worlds setting. Together with adaptively skipping observations that are excessively delayed, it controls changes in the algorithm’s decision distribution without assuming bounded delays. A further procedure connects ordinary regret, which measures accumulated decision loss, with the drifted regret used in the analysis.

The conceptual result concerns how to measure the difficulty created by delayed feedback. The paper identifies the number of observations still outstanding when a decision is made as the relevant quantity, rather than simply how long individual observations take to arrive. This provides a way to analyze learning that remains useful even when a few feedback delays are exceptionally large.
neurips-2024-a-best-of-both-worlds-algor.tldr: A delayed-feedback bandit algorithm tolerates extreme delays by adapting to outstanding information and selectively skipping excessively late observations.

paragraphs: Decision confidence is a person’s assessment of a choice they have made. Computational accounts often address restricted situations, such as choosing between options with equal value. This paper develops a normative framework intended to explain confidence across a wider variety of tasks and experimental arrangements, providing a common account that can apply beyond those specialized settings.

The authors connect their confidence model to planning as inference. In that formulation, the objective combines the reward obtained with the information entropy of the policy, which describes how choices are distributed across available actions. This connection gives the confidence framework a theoretical relationship to an explicit decision objective, linking self-assessment to the process of choosing actions.

The paper also tests the framework against confidence reports from two psychophysics experiments. The authors report that it explains participants’ responses better than the alternative approaches they compare. Together, the theoretical connection and experimental results support the framework as a broader account of decision confidence, with empirical evidence coming from those two experimental settings.
neurips-2024-a-unifying-normative-framew.tldr: A general framework links decision confidence to reward and policy entropy and better explains confidence reports in two experiments.

paragraphs: Spatial audio should change consistently as a listener moves through a virtual scene. Approaches that generate audio from rendered images can inherit visual artifacts and may have to wait for each image to finish rendering. AV-Cloud instead learns a scene representation that supports viewpoint-specific audio generation without requiring a rendered image of that viewpoint.

The representation consists of sparse audio-visual anchor points derived from camera calibration. A module called Audio-Visual Cloud Splatting decodes these anchors into a spatial audio transfer function for the listener’s location. A rendering head then applies that function to monaural sound, producing spatial audio matched to the chosen viewpoint. The shared scene representation makes synchronization possible without explicitly conditioning audio on visual rendering.

The authors demonstrate real-time navigation with both visual and audio content, presenting immersive virtual tourism as an application. On two real-world datasets, they report improvements over existing leading methods in audio reconstruction accuracy, perceptual quality, and acoustic effects. They also report better performance on scenes encountered in the wild, supporting the approach beyond the principal dataset evaluations.
neurips-2024-av-cloud-spatial-audio-rend.tldr: AV-Cloud renders viewpoint-specific spatial audio from sparse scene anchors without waiting for images to be rendered.

paragraphs: Teaching a robot many tasks often requires substantial collections of expert demonstrations. Collecting those demonstrations is costly because actions must be physically performed. BAKU addresses this challenge through the design of the policy architecture, aiming to extract more useful learning from available demonstrations while supporting multiple tasks within one transformer-based system.

The architecture combines components from offline imitation learning: observation-processing trunks, multiple sensory inputs, action heads, and action chunking. Action chunking organizes outputs into groups of actions. The contribution is the careful combination of these components into a simple architecture for learning robot policies, with attention to how observations become actions across different tasks.

Across 129 simulated tasks from LIBERO, Meta-World, and the DeepMind Control suite, the authors report an overall absolute improvement of 18% over RT-1 and MT-ACT, and a 36% improvement on the harder LIBERO benchmark. On 30 real-world manipulation tasks, BAKU reaches 91% success with an average of 17 demonstrations per task. These results support its effectiveness in the evaluated settings where demonstrations are relatively scarce.
neurips-2024-baku-an-efficient-transform.tldr: BAKU combines transformer policy components to improve multitask robot learning, achieving 91% success on 30 real-world tasks.

paragraphs: Many graph benchmarks ask language models to reason directly over a textual description of nodes and connections. This limits evaluation to small graphs. ProGraph changes the task format: models are expected to solve graph problems by writing programs, following the library-based workflow that human specialists use to analyze graphs at different scales.

The manually constructed benchmark contains three categories of graph tasks. Initial evaluations find substantial difficulty, with the best tested model reaching only 36% accuracy. To improve performance, the authors create LLM4Graph, a collection of retrieved documentation and automatically generated code covering six widely used graph libraries. These resources target the practical knowledge needed to turn graph questions into working programs.

The authors use document retrieval to augment closed-source models and fine-tune open-source models on the generated code. They report absolute accuracy improvements of 11–32%. The results show that programming-based graph analysis remains challenging for the evaluated models, while also demonstrating that library documentation and task-related code can materially improve their ability to handle structured graph data.
neurips-2024-can-large-language-models-a.tldr: ProGraph tests graph analysis through programming, while graph-library documentation and code improve model accuracy by 11–32 percentage points.

paragraphs: Selecting useful training data becomes more difficult when organizations collaborate without directly sharing their private datasets. CLUES proposes a quality signal based on how individual examples influence model training. Its guiding premise is that higher-quality examples are more likely to produce training dynamics similar to those produced by a chosen anchor dataset.

The method computes per-example gradients for private data and anchor data. It measures their relationship using the trace of accumulated inner products, turning alignment in training influence into a data-selection score. Selected examples contribute to collaborative fine-tuning, with the server updating the central model through either model merging or federated learning.

The authors also develop an evaluation for data quality control in collaborative settings with heterogeneous medical data. Experiments span medical, multilingual, and financial domains, where training on CLUES-selected data often outperforms other selection methods. The findings support gradient-based agreement with anchor data as a useful selection criterion across the tested settings, while retaining the qualified result that improvements occur often rather than universally.
neurips-2024-clues-collaborative-private.tldr: CLUES selects private-domain training examples by comparing their gradient-based influence with an anchor dataset during collaborative fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Understanding a comic page involves more than finding objects or reading text. A model may need to identify who is speaking, recognize a recurring character, determine reading order, and connect dialogue with visual content. CoMix brings these capabilities into a shared benchmark, addressing the limited size, stylistic range, and task coverage of earlier evaluations.

The benchmark expands annotations in three existing datasets and adds a collection of American-style comic books to reduce the dominance of manga. Its tasks include object detection, speaker identification, character re-identification, reading order, character naming, and dialogue generation. Models are evaluated without task-specific training or with limited fine-tuning, allowing researchers to examine transfer across both tasks and comic styles.

Comparisons between people and leading models reveal a substantial performance gap. This indicates that the tested systems still struggle with the combined visual, textual, and narrative demands captured by the benchmark. A public validation split and an evaluation server for held-out test data provide a common basis for measuring future progress on this broader set of comic-understanding abilities.
neurips-2024-comix-a-comprehensive-bench.tldr: CoMix evaluates diverse comic-understanding tasks and styles, revealing a substantial gap between humans and leading models.

paragraphs: Removing explicit statements from training data may leave clues distributed across other documents. This paper investigates whether language models can combine such clues during learning, identify an unstated structure, and later use it without examples supplied in the prompt. The authors call this ability inductive out-of-context reasoning and study it through five tasks.

In one experiment, a model is fine-tuned only on distances between an unnamed city and known cities. It subsequently identifies the unnamed city as Paris and answers questions using that identity, without in-context examples or chain-of-thought prompting. Other experiments train models on individual coin-flip outcomes or input-output pairs, after which they can describe a coin’s bias or articulate a function and compute its inverses.

The findings establish that frontier models can perform this kind of inference in several settings. However, success is unreliable, especially when smaller models must learn complex structures. The safety implication is therefore a potential obstacle: filtering explicit knowledge may not fully control what a model acquires when enough indirect evidence remains scattered through training data.
neurips-2024-connecting-the-dots-llms-ca.tldr: Language models can sometimes infer and state hidden structure from scattered training evidence, complicating attempts to control knowledge through filtering.

paragraphs: Training-data selection often evaluates examples separately, but examples can affect one another’s usefulness within a batch. This paper studies that interaction in multimodal contrastive learning. It shows that selecting groups of examples according to their joint learnability can accelerate training more effectively than prioritizing each example independently.

The proposed method, JEST, derives a tractable batch-selection algorithm from the dependencies exposed by the contrastive objective. It selects training batches from larger candidate super-batches. Because scoring larger pools adds computational work, the method also uses model approximation to reduce that overhead. Pretrained reference models guide selection toward the distribution of smaller, carefully curated datasets.

The authors report surpassing leading pretraining methods with up to 13 times fewer iterations and 10 times less computation. These are reported best-case reductions, rather than fixed savings for every training run. The reference models’ guidance is essential to the stated performance, showing how a relatively small curated dataset can shape the use of a larger collection and make data selection an additional factor in scaling model training.
neurips-2024-data-curation-via-joint-exa.tldr: JEST jointly selects multimodal training batches, reporting strong pretraining results with up to 10 times less computation.

paragraphs: Video semantic segmentation assigns a category to each image pixel, but adverse weather can degrade frames and cause incorrect predictions. This paper develops an end-to-end domain-adaptation approach that combines information across time with information within the current frame. The aim is to improve segmentation when the target videos contain weather degradation.

A trainable fusion block combines features from adjacent frames without requiring pretrained optical flow. The learning setup uses two teachers: one emphasizes temporal information from neighboring frames, while the other emphasizes spatial information in the current frame. The method also applies weather-degradation augmentation to consecutive frames, so the training inputs better represent how adverse weather affects a video sequence.

On adaptation from VIPER to MVSS, the method achieves 25.4 mean intersection-over-union, improving on the existing leading method by 4.3 points. For Synthia to MVSS, it reaches 33.0, an improvement of 5.8 points. These results support the combined use of temporal feature fusion, complementary teachers, and sequence-level weather augmentation in the two reported adaptation settings.
neurips-2024-end-to-end-video-semantic-s.tldr: Temporal feature fusion, two complementary teachers, and weather augmentation improve video segmentation in two adverse-weather adaptation benchmarks.

paragraphs: Minimax learning problems optimize against an opposing objective and appear in applications including adversarial generation and distributionally robust learning. Simple gradient descent-ascent methods are common, but their practical use has outpaced guarantees about how reliably they converge in stochastic, nonconvex settings. This paper supplies high-probability complexity guarantees for a particular class of these problems.

The analysis assumes a smooth objective satisfying the Polyak–Łojasiewicz condition in the dual variable, together with light-tailed stochastic gradients. Under these conditions, a smoothed alternating gradient descent-ascent method reaches an approximate stationary point with a user-specified success probability. The bound tracks gradient smoothness, conditioning, gradient variance, target accuracy, and the allowed probability of failure.

This gives a quantitative statement about how many stochastic gradient calls suffice with high probability, rather than only describing average behavior. The claimed guarantee applies to the specified nonconvex/PL setting. Numerical studies on a synthetic problem and distributionally robust optimization with real data illustrate the theoretical findings, linking the analysis to concrete optimization examples.
neurips-2024-high-probability-complexity.tldr: Under smoothness, dual PL, and light-tailed-gradient assumptions, smoothed alternating descent-ascent gains high-probability convergence complexity guarantees.

paragraphs: Hyperbolic geometry has been used to represent data and structures learned without supervision. This paper develops a way to embed supervised models themselves, with particular attention to decision trees and ensembles. Its aim is to give these models a geometric representation that supports clear encoding and visualization in the Poincaré disk.

The first contribution connects losses used for class-probability estimation with hyperbolic embeddings. The second resolves an ambiguity in representing decision trees and ensembles within the disk. Together, these steps connect the learning objectives of supervised prediction to a concrete geometric representation and address how model structures can be placed there unambiguously.

The third contribution modifies the Poincaré distance smoothly to improve representation and visualization near the disk’s boundary, a region especially important for this application. The modification preserves hyperbolicity and rests on a generalization of the fundamental theorem of calculus. The result is a mathematical framework for representing supervised models, with a distance construction that the authors also identify as independently interesting.
neurips-2024-hyperbolic-embeddings-of-su.tldr: The paper develops hyperbolic representations of supervised models and a modified distance that improves encoding near the Poincaré disk’s boundary.

paragraphs: Temporal link prediction uses past interactions to predict future connections between entities. Relative encodings help models describe relationships between entities, but constructing them can be expensive, and existing approaches often emphasize connectivity while making limited use of time. This paper develops a unified way to understand these encodings through temporal walk matrices.

Building on that analysis, the authors introduce TPNet, a temporal graph neural network. Its temporal walk matrix includes time decay, allowing the representation to account for both graph structure and when interactions occurred. A random-feature propagation mechanism maintains the relevant matrix information implicitly, with theoretical guarantees, improving computational and storage efficiency.

The connection to temporal walk matrices supplies a principled basis for analyzing existing encodings and designing new ones. Experiments on 13 benchmark datasets evaluate both predictive effectiveness and efficiency. TPNet outperforms the compared baselines on most datasets and reaches a maximum speedup of 33.3 times against the leading baseline. The reported speedup is a maximum observed result, while the accuracy gains hold across most of the evaluated datasets.
neurips-2024-improving-temporal-link-pre.tldr: TPNet combines time-aware graph encodings with efficient random-feature propagation, improving most benchmark results and achieving up to 33.3 times speedup.

paragraphs: Differentially private estimation must protect individual data while producing useful numerical answers. This paper proposes a framework that adapts to how difficult the particular dataset is. It builds on inverse sensitivity, which assesses candidate outputs through how close the observed dataset is to datasets that would produce those outputs.

The authors adjust that closeness measure and use the sparse vector technique for an efficient implementation. They also relax a restriction from earlier instance-optimality results: the most likely output need not match the underlying data’s answer. This allows a more flexible balance between bias and variance and enables the method to extend to unbounded data.

The framework is especially suited to asymmetric cases, where movement toward different candidate answers involves different distances from the observed dataset. The authors provide theory and empirical evidence for this advantage. They instantiate the method in linear time for variance and common classification and regression performance metrics, reporting substantially better private estimates in their experiments. The contribution connects dataset-specific asymmetry with a practical choice of estimation tradeoff.
neurips-2024-instance-specific-asymmetri.tldr: A private-estimation framework uses dataset-specific asymmetry and a flexible bias–variance tradeoff to improve estimates efficiently.

paragraphs: Multimodal language models can understand images broadly while struggling with the meaning of precise points on an object. This paper introduces Semantic Keypoint Comprehension to study that gap. The challenge covers understanding a keypoint’s meaning, locating keypoints from visual prompts, and locating them from textual prompts.

KptLLM addresses these tasks with a unified model built around an identify-then-detect strategy. It first determines the semantic identity of the requested keypoint and then uses a chain-of-thought process to determine its position. Purpose-designed modules accommodate different input modalities and support both semantic interpretation and localization. This organization makes identifying what a point represents an explicit part of finding where it is.

The authors report superior performance across multiple keypoint-detection benchmarks, alongside semantic capabilities for interpreting keypoints. These findings support evaluating fine-grained image understanding through both location and meaning. The contribution is therefore twofold: a broader task definition for keypoint comprehension and a model that connects language-based interpretation with precise visual detection.
neurips-2024-kptllm-unveiling-the-power-.tldr: KptLLM first identifies a keypoint’s meaning and then locates it, unifying semantic understanding with text- and image-prompted detection.

paragraphs: A model that fits a large accelerator cluster may be unsuitable for a mobile device, yet separately training many sizes is expensive. MatFormer addresses this mismatch by placing feed-forward networks of different sizes inside one transformer as nested blocks. Training optimizes several nested sizes together, allowing hundreds of smaller models to be extracted without additional computation for that extraction.

The authors evaluate this approach for language and vision, using both decoder and encoder models. From an 850-million-parameter language model, they extract models ranging from 582 million to 850 million parameters. These models achieve better validation loss and one-shot downstream evaluations than independently trained counterparts.

For vision encoders, extracted smaller models preserve the metric-space structure used for retrieval, supporting adaptation of retrieval systems to different resource budgets. The authors also show that accurate, consistent submodels can significantly reduce inference latency through speculative decoding. Together, the findings support a single trained model family that offers multiple deployment choices while retaining useful relationships among its smaller and larger members.
neurips-2024-matformer-nested-transforme.tldr: MatFormer trains nested transformer components together so one model can supply accurate submodels for different inference budgets.

paragraphs: Knowledge graphs express facts as relationships between entities. This paper asks whether a language model can learn to work directly in a specialized language for those facts. Each sentence contains exactly three elements: a starting entity, a relation, and an ending entity. That restricted structure gives the model a precise format for expressing graph relationships.

The unfamiliar entity and relation vocabulary is taught through a tailored dictionary and example sentences. The approach also retrieves relevant graph context in real time and augments the embeddings of tokens in the specialized language. These additions connect the model’s interpretation of a sentence with the surrounding knowledge graph, supporting understanding of both individual terms and their relationships.

The authors report that the resulting model learns this graph language and substantially reduces completion errors compared with conventional knowledge-graph embedding methods. It can also generate accurate three-element sentences from a supplied starting entity and interpret previously unseen graph terms. The findings support combining language-model learning with a deliberately constrained representation of structured facts.
neurips-2024-mkgl-mastery-of-a-three-wor.tldr: MKGL teaches language models a three-element knowledge-graph language using dictionaries, examples, retrieved context, and augmented token embeddings.

paragraphs: An embodied agent must reason about a scene in relation to its current situation. Existing datasets provide limited coverage of the modalities, scenarios, and scale needed to evaluate that ability. This paper introduces MSQA, a situated question-answering dataset containing 251,000 question-answer pairs across nine categories and diverse real-world three-dimensional scenes.

The collection process uses 3D scene graphs and vision-language models. The benchmark interleaves text, images, and point clouds when describing situations and questions, aiming to reduce ambiguity that can arise from a single input modality. A second benchmark, MSNN, evaluates next-step navigation, focusing on how models connect actions with transitions between situations.

Evaluations of reasoning and navigation expose limitations in existing vision-language models and emphasize the importance of explicitly modeling situations and handling mixed input formats. Experiments on data scaling and transfer across domains also support MSQA’s usefulness as pretraining data. The work therefore provides both a broader evaluation of situated understanding and evidence that its dataset can help train more capable models.
neurips-2024-multi-modal-situated-reason.tldr: MSQA and MSNN evaluate situated 3D reasoning and navigation with interleaved text, images, and point clouds.

paragraphs: Changing an object’s lighting from one image requires reasoning about its shape, materials, and illumination. Neural Gaffer approaches this task with an end-to-end diffusion model that receives the object image and a target environment map. The map specifies the desired lighting, guiding generation of a relit image without explicitly decomposing the scene into geometry and material components.

The authors start from a pretrained diffusion model and fine-tune it on synthetic relighting data. Their approach draws on lighting knowledge already present in the image generator, adapting it for controlled relighting. It is designed to handle general objects and new environmental lighting conditions, extending beyond methods restricted to particular image categories or special capture procedures.

Evaluations on synthetic images and Internet imagery show advantages in accuracy and generalization. The authors also combine the model with other generative methods for text-directed relighting and object insertion. For 3D applications, it can serve as a relighting prior, including for radiance fields. These uses demonstrate how the learned image-level lighting transformation can support several related editing workflows.
neurips-2024-neural-gaffer-relighting-an.tldr: Neural Gaffer fine-tunes a diffusion model to relight objects from one image using a target environment map.

paragraphs: Simple bilevel optimization asks for the best solution to one objective among the solutions that already minimize another. This paper considers convex objectives at both levels. The challenge is to improve the upper-level objective while respecting lower-level optimality, with a quantitative guarantee on how much computation an approximate solution requires.

The authors introduce a penalty framework that relates approximate solutions of reformulated problems to approximate solutions of the original bilevel problem. Different smoothness and convexity assumptions lead to different applicable algorithms and complexity results. For composite convex objectives, an alpha-Hölderian error bound and additional mild assumptions yield an iteration bound of order epsilon raised to minus one-half of the maximum of alpha and beta, for any positive beta.

That result provides paired accuracy tolerances of epsilon and epsilon raised to beta. The bound improves further when the smooth component of the upper-level objective is strongly convex. The authors also establish complexity results for general nonsmooth objectives and report numerical experiments demonstrating effectiveness. The contribution makes the relationship among structural assumptions, solution accuracy, and computational effort explicit.
neurips-2024-penalty-based-methods-for-s.tldr: A penalty framework gives finite-iteration guarantees for convex bilevel optimization under Hölderian error bounds and related assumptions.

paragraphs: Learning across measurement types often relies on paired observations of the same sample. In biology, some measurements destroy the sample, making such pairing difficult. This paper proposes aligning unpaired observations by using information about experimental treatments, drawing a connection between missing views in multimodal data and potential outcomes in causal inference.

The approach assumes that samples have been experimentally perturbed by treatments. It estimates a propensity score separately from each modality and uses these scores to define distances between samples. The authors show that the score captures all information shared between the latent state and treatment. This supplies a common matching basis tied to treatment-related information across otherwise different measurement spaces.

The paper evaluates shared-nearest-neighbor and optimal-transport matching using that distance. Optimal transport produces significant improvements over leading alignment approaches on synthetic tasks, data from the NeurIPS Multimodal Single-Cell Integration Challenge, and a microscopy-to-expression prediction task. These results support treatment-derived propensity scores as useful alignment signals in the experimentally perturbed settings studied.
neurips-2024-propensity-score-alignment-.tldr: Treatment-derived propensity scores provide a shared distance for aligning unpaired modalities, with strong results using optimal-transport matching.

paragraphs: Unsupervised object discovery requires a model to group image features into distinct objects without object labels. Synchrony-based approaches represent these groupings through phase relationships in complex-valued activations. SynCx extends this idea by using complex-valued weights and a recurrent architecture, allowing the representation to be revised over multiple iterations.

The model is a fully convolutional autoencoder whose hidden bottleneck captures regular arrangements of features in particular phase relationships. Repeated updates propagate local constraints until the phase assignments form a globally consistent configuration. Object binding happens through multiplication between complex-valued weights and activations, avoiding the additional binding mechanisms used by existing synchrony-based approaches.

The authors report that SynCx outperforms or remains strongly competitive with current models on unsupervised object discovery. It also avoids certain systematic grouping errors, including difficulty separating similarly colored objects without extra supervision. The findings support recurrence and complex-valued computation as useful ingredients for coordinating local feature groupings into coherent object representations.
neurips-2024-recurrent-complex-weighted-.tldr: SynCx uses recurrent complex-valued computation to discover objects and avoid grouping errors such as merging similarly colored objects.

paragraphs: Chip placement arranges circuit modules and affects power, performance, and area. Reinforcement-learning approaches that build layouts from scratch can face long training, weak generalization, and inaccurate rewards. This paper changes the policy’s role: it learns to adjust an existing placement, using the information already available in that layout.

Working at the refinement stage provides the policy with more informative context and relatively dense, precise rewards. The training process also includes placement regularity, which the authors identify as important in chip design but often overlooked by reinforcement-learning placement methods. The resulting regulator is designed to fine-tune layouts produced by any placement method.

The authors compare global half-perimeter wirelength and regularity on the ISPD 2005 and ICCAD 2015 benchmarks against competitive approaches. They also assess power, performance, and area with commercial software, reporting significant improvements. These findings support refinement as a productive role for reinforcement learning in placement, with the policy improving an available layout and being evaluated on downstream chip-design outcomes.
neurips-2024-reinforcement-learning-poli.tldr: A reinforcement-learning regulator refines existing chip placements using informative rewards and regularity, yielding reported power, performance, and area improvements.

paragraphs: A vision-language model’s perception and problem-solving scores provide only part of its performance profile. VHELM extends the HELM evaluation framework to cover nine aspects: perception, knowledge, reasoning, bias, fairness, multilinguality, robustness, toxicity, and safety. It brings existing datasets together to make these different dimensions visible within one evaluation framework.

The framework standardizes inference settings, prompting procedures, and evaluation metrics, improving the comparability of model results. Its evaluation process is designed to be automatic, lightweight, and inexpensive. The initial assessment covers 22 models across 21 datasets, producing a multidimensional snapshot rather than relying on a narrow selection of capability tests.

One reported finding is that efficiency-oriented models perform significantly worse than their larger counterparts on the bias benchmark, without the same pattern appearing across the other evaluated aspects. This illustrates why broad evaluation can reveal differences that conventional capability measures miss. The authors release raw generations and complete results for transparency and intend VHELM to expand with additional datasets and models over time.
neurips-2024-vhelm-a-holistic-evaluation.tldr: VHELM standardizes vision-language evaluation across nine dimensions, revealing model differences that capability-focused benchmarks can miss.

paragraphs: Image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval benchmarks can appear nearly solved while offering limited evidence about performance on unfamiliar domains. The authors argue that transferring between COCO and Flickr is an insufficient test because their images and language are highly similar. WikiDO introduces more varied topics and geographic coverage to evaluate this generalization challenge.

The benchmark contains 380,000 Wikipedia image-text pairs with domain labels, plus human-verified in-distribution and out-of-distribution test sets of 3,000 pairs each. The authors evaluate models of different capacities and examine how training objectives and dataset sizes affect transfer. This setup distinguishes improvement on familiar domains from improvement on held-out domains.

BLIP-2 achieves approximately 66% recall at rank one on WikiDO’s out-of-distribution test, compared with about 81% on COCO and 95% on Flickr. Fine-tuning on WikiDO improves out-of-distribution recall by at most approximately 5%, versus approximately 12% on in-distribution examples. These reported differences show that better performance within the training distribution does not translate into equally large gains on unfamiliar domains in this evaluation.
neurips-2024-wikido-a-new-benchmark-eval.tldr: WikiDO uses diverse Wikipedia image-text pairs to expose retrieval generalization gaps obscured by familiar benchmarks.
